summary.against_the_decision: In scope: N = 2^17, r = 8, p = 1, the form `scrypt$17$8$1$`, maxmem 160 MiB (N2a, О15), and the bundled common-password refusal counted under criterion 1 with PW-4, SU-5 and RS-2 (N2b, О16). Nothing outside the Addition was added.

findings.criterion: 1 and the description «Mechanics» against guard row (6)
findings.problem: The amendment fixes the list as app/server/auth/common-passwords.txt. app/test/unit/import-boundaries.test.js `fileFindings` (lines 738-749) reports every tracked file under server/, api/ or worker/ that does not end in .js («a file that is not .js: …», its own planted case server/notes.txt, lines 1672-1691), and IB-1 (line 751) asserts the real tree has no finding. So the named file turns IB-1 red, while guard row (6) of REQ-114 says import-boundaries.test.js stays unchanged (the code design's row A21 says the same).
findings.fix: Either keep the list as data in a .js module under app/server/auth/ (and name that path in criterion 1 and the description), or put the .txt file in a folder outside those rules that the Vercel upload keeps, or change guard row (6) to a was → became row that names the one exception for that file in fileFindings.

findings.problem: «the same refusal with unchanged row counts holds at setup (SU-5 …), at the password change and at a reset link (RS-2 …)»: the password change has no test name or file.
findings.fix: Name the test of the password change (for example a case of app/test/int/auth-session.test.js, as the code design gives it).

findings.problem: docs/program/public-v1/ARCHITECTURE.md line 249 still says N = 2^15 and `scrypt$15$8$1$`; PROGRESS.md «Plan amendments» has no row for the change (grep of scrypt and 2^17 in PROGRESS.md → no line); the code design lists it as to be recorded (line 1198).
findings.fix: ORCH adds the plan-amendment row (no block edit).

findings.problem: Accepting an invite takes «a password by the rules of REQ-114», so the common-password refusal applies there too, but no test of REQ-116 names it.
findings.fix: At the REQ-116 code design, add the case to invites.test.js (or say the rule is reached only through the one password module that PW-4 tests).
